Original Requirements: The VLA Expansion Project Correlator Monitor and Control System (CCS) must provide the physical link between WIDAR Correlator hardware and the VLA Expansion Project monitor and control system. It requires a Master/Slave network architecture, autonomous fault recovery, real-time data processing, secure remote access, and high reliability/uptime. The system must handle configuration translation, health monitoring, hardware testing, and support redundant critical areas with hot-swappable components.
Product Goals: Ensure maximum uptime and reliability for astronomical data processing
Provide modular abstraction for seamless hardware configuration and control
Enable secure, role-based remote access and autonomous fault recovery
User Stories: As a system operator, I want to configure correlator hardware via a Virtual Correlator Interface so that I can manage observations without direct hardware manipulation.
As a maintenance engineer, I want the system to automatically attempt recovery from hardware faults so that operational downtime is minimized.
As a software developer, I want remote access to system logs and debugging tools so that I can troubleshoot issues outside of working hours.
As a security administrator, I want to manage user access levels and audit all login attempts so that unauthorized access is prevented.
As a scientist, I want real-time visibility into correlator health states so that I can ensure data integrity during experiments.
Competitive Analysis: ALMA Correlator Control System: Highly specialized for radio astronomy, similar scale but different architecture.
SKA Control System: Next-generation array control, focuses on massive scalability.
EPICS Framework: Open-source industrial control framework, widely used in physics but requires customization.
Siemens SCADA Systems: Robust industrial control, lacks specific astronomical hardware integration.
NASA DSN Control Systems: High reliability for deep space, similar redundancy requirements.
VLA Legacy System: Predecessor system, proven but lacks modern modularity and automation.
Generic Master/Slave PLC Systems: Cost-effective industrial solution, lacks specific scientific data processing capabilities.

Requirement Analysis: The system demands a robust Master/Slave architecture to isolate real-time hardware control from network loads. Critical requirements include redundancy (Master/Power computers), autonomous self-healing (watchdogs, reboot logic), and strict security (authentication, logging). The interface must support both automated system commands and human GUI interaction via the Virtual Correlator Interface. Hardware constraints include specific network speeds (100Mbit+), UPS integration, and hot-swappable CMIB modules. The software must be modular, debuggable, and support standalone operation.
Requirement Pool: Implement Master/Slave network architecture with redundant communication paths
Develop autonomous fault recovery mechanisms including watchdog timers and auto-reboot
Establish secure user authentication, access control levels, and audit logging
Create Virtual Correlator Interface (VCI) for configuration and monitoring
Ensure CMIB modules support hot-swapping and unique IP addressing
UI Design draft: The UI will feature a dashboard displaying real-time correlator health status, error logs, and configuration tables. It will include a navigation menu for System Configuration, Monitoring, Maintenance Tools, and Security Settings. The style should be functional and high-contrast for control room environments, with clear indicators for system states (Green=OK, Red=Fault). Remote access capabilities will be integrated via secure web or client-server interface.
